subject: Meteorology
title: Rayleigh Scattering
description: A quick win: understand Rayleigh Scattering.

hook.text: Rayleigh scattering is why the sky is blue—air molecules scatter short wavelengths of light much more than long ones.

buildup.text: Blue and violet light scatter about 10 times more than red—scattering intensity follows the fourth power of frequency.

discovery.text: The sky looks blue rather than violet because our eyes are more sensitive to blue—and sunlight has less violet.

twist.text: At sunrise and sunset, light travels through much more atmosphere—blue is scattered away, leaving reds and oranges.

climax.text: Lord Rayleigh explained this in 1871—solving a question that had puzzled thinkers since antiquity.

punchline.text: Blue scatters most—so the sky wears blue all day.

quiz.question: Why does Rayleigh scattering make the sky blue rather than violet?
options: Our eyes are more sensitive to blue
Violet is absorbed by ozone only
